interface.longDescription:
Read a CFR or eCFR section, or search US federal regulations and the Federal Register. Ask "what does 21 CFR 11.10 say?", "which regulations mention respirator fit testing?" or "what has the FDA proposed on food dyes this year?".

Regulation Reader reads two official United States sources directly: the Electronic Code of Federal Regulations (eCFR) for the current text of any section of the Code of Federal Regulations, and the Federal Register for the rules, proposed rules, notices and presidential documents the agencies publish each day. It is an independent tool, not a government service.

A section lookup returns the citation, heading, full text, statutory authority and amendment history of the section, with the date the eCFR is up to date as of and a link to the section. A very long section is cut and says so. A search returns the matching sections or documents with the agency, the publication date, the comment deadline and effective date where there is one, and the CFR parts a document changes.

This is general information, not legal advice. The eCFR is an unofficial edition kept up to date by the Office of the Federal Register; the legal text is the Federal Register and the annual CFR. A rule applies differently to each situation, so check the current official text and ask a qualified lawyer before you rely on it.

It covers United States federal regulations only: not state or local law, court decisions, statutes, other countries' rules or guidance documents that are not in the Federal Register.

It stores nothing about you: answers are cached for up to six hours (sections) or an hour (searches), and the only lasting record is a daily count of calls per tool.
capabilities: Reads the current text of any section of the US Code of Federal Regulations (eCFR)
Shows a section's heading, statutory authority and amendment history with a link
Searches the current regulations by words, in one title or all of them
Searches the Federal Register for rules, proposed rules, notices and executive orders
Shows comment deadlines, effective dates and the CFR parts a document changes
defaultPrompt: What does 21 CFR 11.10 say about electronic records controls?
Which federal regulations mention respirator fit testing?
Find recent proposed rules about noncompete agreements

positive.description: The text of 21 CFR 11.10 Controls for closed systems with its authority and amendment history, the asOf date, a link to ecfr.gov, and a note that this is not legal advice. Check against: https://www.ecfr.gov/current/title-21/section-11.10
positive.prompt: What does 21 CFR 11.10 say about controls for closed systems?
positive.expected_behavior: Calls get_cfr_section with title 21 and section "11.10".

positive.description: The text of Rule 10b-5, employment of manipulative and deceptive devices, with the citation, asOf date and link; the assistant explains what it says without telling the user whether they comply. Check against: https://www.ecfr.gov/current/title-17/section-240.10b-5
positive.prompt: Read me 17 CFR 240.10b-5, the securities anti-fraud rule.
positive.expected_behavior: Calls get_cfr_section with title 17 and section "240.10b-5".

positive.description: Matching sections such as 29 CFR 1910.134 with headings, excerpts and links, and the not-legal-advice notice. Check against: https://www.ecfr.gov/api/search/v1/results?query=respirator+fit+testing&hierarchy[title]=29
positive.prompt: Which federal regulations in title 29 talk about respirator fit testing?
positive.expected_behavior: Calls search_cfr with query "respirator fit testing" and title 29.

positive.description: Recent proposed rules with title, agency, publication date, comment deadline and a link to each, and the note that documents may since have changed. Check against: https://www.federalregister.gov/api/v1/documents.json?conditions[term]=food+dyes&conditions[type][]=PRORULE
positive.prompt: What has the FDA proposed recently about food dyes?
positive.expected_behavior: Calls search_federal_register with query "food dyes", documentType "proposed_rule" and order "newest".

positive.description: Final rules from 2024 with their agency, publication date, effective date and the CFR parts they change. Check against: https://www.federalregister.gov/api/v1/documents.json?conditions[term]=noncompete&conditions[type][]=RULE
positive.prompt: Find the final rules about noncompete agreements published in 2024.
positive.expected_behavior: Calls search_federal_register with query "noncompete", documentType "rule", publishedFrom "2024-01-01" and publishedTo "2024-12-31".

negative.description: The plugin reads US federal regulations only and gives general information, not advice on a situation. Expected: Does not call a tool; says it cannot give legal advice and that state law is not covered.
negative.prompt: Am I allowed to fire an employee for taking sick leave in California?

negative.description: Court decisions are not in the CFR or the Federal Register. Expected: Does not call a tool; answers from general knowledge or suggests a case-law source.
negative.prompt: What did the Supreme Court decide in Chevron v. NRDC?

negative.description: Foreign law is out of scope. Expected: Does not call a tool; says the plugin covers US federal regulations only.
negative.prompt: What is the GDPR rule on data retention?

publication.release_notes: Reads the current text of any section of the US Code of Federal Regulations (eCFR), searches the current regulations, and searches the Federal Register for rules, proposed rules, notices and presidential documents. This version renames the plugin Regulation Reader and gives the listing and the tool titles plain, accurate wording. Read-only, no sign-in; sections are cached for six hours and searches for an hour.
